title: Endo-1,4-β-D-xylanase Assay Using Azo-Xylan and Variants Thereof
author: Luca Bombardi

steps.title: Prepare Azo‑Xylan substrate (1% w/v)
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g Azo‑Xylan powder, add to 80 mL boiling distilled water in a hot‑plate stirrer, stir vigorously until fully suspended, turn off heat, continue stirring until the suspension is homogeneous, then add distilled water to a final volume of 100 mL (final concentration 1 % w/v).

steps.title: Prepare citrate buffer (pH 3‑5)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 9.60 g citric acid (2.63 M) in 80 mL distilled water, adjust the pH to 3.0, 4.0 or 5.0 with 6 N HCl, then bring the volume to 100 mL with distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare sodium phosphate buffer pH 6.0
steps.instruction: Mix 43.80 mL of 1 M NaH₂PO₄ (final 438 mM) with 6.20 mL of 1 M Na₂HPO₄ (final 62 mM), add distilled water to 100 mL total.

steps.title: Prepare sodium phosphate buffer pH 7.0
steps.instruction: Mix 19.50 mL of 1 M NaH₂PO₄ (final 195 mM) with 30.50 mL of 1 M Na₂HPO₄ (final 305 mM), add distilled water to 100 mL total.

steps.title: Prepare sodium phosphate buffer pH 8.0
steps.instruction: Mix 3.40 mL of 1 M NaH₂PO₄ (final 34 mM) with 46.60 mL of 1 M Na₂HPO₄ (final 466 mM), add distilled water to 100 mL total.

steps.title: Prepare potassium phosphate buffer (pH 6‑7)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6.80 g KH₂PO₄ (0.50 M) in 80 mL distilled water, adjust pH to 6.0 or 7.0 with 6 N HCl, then bring the volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare Tris‑HCl buffer (pH 7‑9)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6.06 g Tris‑base (0.50 M) in 80 mL distilled water, adjust pH to 7.0, 8.0 or 9.0 with 6 N HCl, then bring the volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare CAPS buffer (pH 10‑11)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 11.06 g CAPS powder (0.50 M) in 80 mL distilled water, adjust pH to 10.0 or 11.0 with 5 M NaOH, then bring the volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare precipitant solution (95 % ethanol)
steps.instruction: Mix 100 mL of 95 % (v/v) ethanol; this solution will be used to stop reactions.

steps.title: Standard assay – pre‑incubation
steps.instruction: In 1.5 mL plastic tubes, add 50 µL of the 1 % w/v Azo‑Xylan substrate and 200 µL of each cell‑free supernatant (CFS) in separate tubes; place tubes in a thermo‑shaker and pre‑warm for 5 min at 50 °C under static conditions.

steps.title: Standard assay – start reactions
steps.instruction: Combine 50 µL of each pre‑warmed CFS with 50 µL of the pre‑warmed Azo‑Xylan substrate in a new tube (final reaction volume 100 µL).

steps.title: Standard assay – incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction tubes for 2 h at 50 °C under static conditions.

steps.title: Standard assay – stop reaction
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of the precipitant solution to each tube, vortex briefly, then let the tubes stand at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Standard assay – clarification
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 10 000 × g for 5 min; the supernatant is the clarified reaction mixture.

steps.title: Standard assay – absorbance measurement
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of each clarified supernatant into a well of a 96‑well plate and measure absorbance at 590 nm.

steps.title: Determine optimal temperature
steps.instruction: Repeat the pre‑incubation and incubation steps at a series of temperatures (e.g., 30 °C, 40 °C, 50 °C, 60 °C) to identify the temperature giving maximal activity.

steps.title: Determine optimal pH
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the desired buffer (citrate, phosphate, Tris‑HCl, or CAPS) to 50 µL of Azo‑Xylan substrate, pre‑warm substrates and CFS at the optimum temperature, then start reactions by adding 40 µL of pre‑warmed CFS to the buffered substrate; incubate for 1 h at the optimum temperature.

steps.title: Determine enzyme thermostability
steps.instruction: Pre‑incubate CFS aliquots at the optimum temperature and at 5 °C or 10 °C below it; at defined time points withdraw 40 µL aliquots and assay them under optimum pH and temperature with a 1 h incubation.

steps.title: Determine enzyme storage stability
steps.instruction: Periodically assay CFSs stored at 4 °C using the same pH, temperature, and 1 h incubation conditions as the standard assay to monitor activity over time.

steps.title: Prepare negative controls
steps.instruction: For each assay, mix 250 µL precipitant solution with 50 µL Azo‑Xylan substrate (add 10 µL buffer when performing buffered assays), then add 50 µL CFS (or 40 µL CFS for buffered assays); run all reactions in technical triplicates of each biological triplicate.
